title: feat: Agent source and keep existing priorities
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds Agent as a Dev Source value for items opened by bot accounts (app catalog, API docs, README refresh, failing-workflow issues); issues the Discord relay opens for a person stay Community
- Relayed issues are recognised by the relay's `**Author:** … (UID: …)` line, since the relay and the catalog/docs PRs share the same bot account
- The project manager now fills Priority only when it is empty, so priorities set by people, earlier runs or the Express job are kept
- Drops the separate github-actions list; bot accounts are detected from GitHub's account type

The Dev Source field already has the Agent option.

gist.headline: The board knows its bees
gist.blurb: The project board gets better at telling bot work from community requests. It also leaves priorities alone when someone has already set them.
gist.summary: The project manager assigns Dev Source = Agent to bot-opened items while keeping Discord-relayed issues with an `**Author:** … (UID: …)` line as Community, and fills Priority only when it is empty.
gist.impact: Maintainers get more accurate source labels without overwriting priorities set by people, earlier runs, or the Express job.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy GitHub-style project board has Agent and Community columns, with a small relay note distinguishing a person's request from bot-opened work. Polli, wearing a tiny tool belt, sorts cards while leaving an existing priority stamp untouched; code-plants grow beside the board.
